name: How do Denver area ceiling height codes affect basement ceiling framing?

mainEntity.name: How do Denver area ceiling height codes affect basement ceiling framing?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, building departments enforce local residential codes that require minimum finished ceiling heights, typically at least 7 feet for habitable rooms, with allowances down to 6 feet 4 inches or 6 feet 6 inches under beams and ducts. When framing a basement ceiling in Denver, Centennial, or Parker, careful measurement is critical so that framed soffits around I-beams or duct trunks do not drop below these allowable thresholds. Planning soffit placement precisely ensures your finished remodel complies with regional inspection standards during final sign-off.
acceptedAnswer.description: Regional codes generally require minimum finished ceiling heights of 7 feet in habitable spaces, meaning soffits must be framed tightly around ducts to meet clearance requirements.
